meeting_header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rohan Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions); Ari Kaplan (CTO, Celestial), Priya Nair (ML Eng), Samir Das (Infra), Olivia Park (Product)
summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection for Celestial's multilingual customer support and document automation product. Key concerns: context length (large documents up to 200k tokens), multilingual accuracy (EN/ES/FR/DE/KO), tool/function calling for retrieval and internal tools, and deployment model tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Security/compliance and pilot timeline discussed.
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Rohan our SE and Lena from solutions. Ari, Priya, Samir, Olivia, thanks for making time.

[00:12] Ari Kaplan: Yeah thanks, quick note - we got a few other meetings earlier so we'll be tight on time but excited to talk about model selection. Our main product parses and summarizes very long legal and medical docs and it needs to be multilingual.

[00:25] Priya Nair: And to add, we also need tool-calling to wire in a retrieval system and a set of internal QA tools, function-calls basically. Latency matters but so does cost - we look at throughput for batch jobs and low-latency for interactive annotators.

[00:40] Rohan Patel: Great, that's helpful. Maybe I'll start high-level: we typically help teams choose between a family of open models depending on context-length, latency SLOs, and whether you want hosted, dedicated, or private. For long contexts you mentioned 200k tokens - is that worst-case or typical?

[00:58] Ari Kaplan: Worst-case. Typical is more like 20-30k, but when a customer uploads a full dossier it can spike. We also need to support Spanish and Korean at parity with English for summarization.

[01:12] Samir Das: On infra side, we have strict requirements around data residency and we might prefer VPC/private deployment for the pilot if Redwood supports that - SAML/SSO and KMS integration are must-haves.

[01:27] Lena Ortiz: Absolutely - we have private deployment options with a customer-managed control plane, and we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers. We also provide audit logs and can map to SOC 2 controls. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[01:40] Olivia Park: Curious on the model side - are you recommending a single model that handles everything or a hybrid routing approach?

[01:49] Rohan Patel: We often recommend hybrid routing: a smaller, faster cheaper model for short/interactive requests, and a larger, longer-context model for document-level jobs. Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity is limited.
[02:05] Priya Nair: For the long-context stuff, what are the open models you support with 100k+ or 200k token contexts? We've seen research models but worried about production stability.

[02:18] Maya Chen: We onboard and benchmark multiple open models - a few families support extended context via sparse or segmented attention. For 200k tokens we'd typically look at the 128k and 256k context variants of certain models; we'll share a compatibility matrix. Keep in mind longer context often impacts latency and memory footprint, so Dedicated/Private deployment with tuned kernels can help.
[02:40] Ari Kaplan: And multilingual performance - are some models better out of the box for Spanish/Korean? We can't afford heavy finetuning initially.

[02:49] Rohan Patel: Yes, model families vary. Some open models are trained multilingual and perform decently across languages; others excel in English. We run evals tied to your prompt sets - that's part of Redwood Optimize: we can run a quality comparison on your sample prompts and show token-level cost and accuracy tradeoffs.
[03:05] Priya Nair: Sounds good. On tool-calling, do you support both synchronous function calls and external retriever hooking? How do you handle state and KV cache for long-running sessions?

[03:16] Rohan Patel: We support function/tool calling patterns similar to major APIs, and you can register tools that the model can call. For long-running sessions we manage KV cache and prefix caching to avoid recomputing earlier context. That drastically reduces per-token compute for multi-step interactions.
[03:35] Samir Das: Performance question - for batch summarization of 1000 documents a night, what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated? Ballpark numbers are fine.

[03:46] Maya Chen: Ballpark: Hosted gives fastest time to value but variable unit cost; Dedicated reserved capacity can reduce per-token cost by 30-60% depending on utilization and batching. Redwood Optimize can tune batching/quantization to optimize further. We'll send sample cost models with utilization assumptions.
[04:05] Ari Kaplan: Security - can you confirm SAML SSO, SCIM, customer-managed KMS, and audit trails? Also any HIPAA or other compliance support?

[04:17] Lena Ortiz: SAML/SCIM supported, KMS integrations supported for Private deployments. We provide detailed audit logs and can discuss HIPAA scope in our security pack. For highly regulated workloads we usually recommend Private with on-prem or VPC to reduce the attack surface.

[04:32] Priya Nair: Ok - for benchmarking, we'll need a reproducible harness. Can you run benchmarks against our prompts and give latency p99 and token cost? Also measure multilingual F1 or ROUGE for summarization?

[04:45] Rohan Patel: Yes, we do that. Typical deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost per request, quality metrics on your evaluation set, and recommendations for model + quantization profile. We'll schedule a 2-hour technical session to run this with your team.
[05:00] Olivia Park: Timeline - we'd like to run a 4-week pilot and make a decision in Q4. Is that feasible?

[05:07] Maya Chen: Definitely feasible. Pilot usually is 2-6 weeks depending on scope. Next steps from our side: send pricing, security docs, provision pilot workspace, and Rohan will coordinate benchmarks.
[05:20] Ari Kaplan: One more thing - do you have any customers using Redwood for similar long-document multilingual workflows? Case studies help.
[05:27] Lena Ortiz: We have anonymized case studies we can share; some customers in legal and healthcare use long-context summarization on dedicated infra. I'll include those links.
[05:35] Priya Nair: On the technical deep-dive, can we test both model families and a hybrid routing strategy? We want to see routing thresholds and the cost/latency tradeoffs.

[05:45] Rohan Patel: Absolutely - we'll set up experiments with short-model fallback and long-context model, and measure routing latencies plus cost. Also we'll test function-calling integration with your retriever.
[05:58] Samir Das: A practical question: if we go Private, what is the expected lead time for an on-prem deployment vs VPC?

[06:06] Lena Ortiz: VPC deployment can be done in a few weeks with automated scripts; on-prem lead time is longer because of network/ops approvals - typically 6-10 weeks depending on scope. We'll bring in our deployment team when we get to that stage.
[06:20] Maya Chen: Great - I'll recap action items at the end. Any other blockers?
[06:26] Ari Kaplan: None from our side. We'll put together the prompt set and data sample this afternoon.
[06:31] Maya Chen: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items we discussed. End call.
[06:36] -- End of recording --
